one_liner: Pure C# Lua 5.2 interpreter for .NET and Unity with low-overhead C# interop; beats NLua and MoonSharp on host-call loops.
what_it_does: Lua-CSharp is a Lua 5.2 interpreter written entirely in managed C#, shipped as the LuaCSharp NuGet package and a Unity package. You create a LuaState, run code with DoStringAsync/DoFileAsync, exchange LuaValue/LuaTable values through state.Environment, and expose C# functions as LuaFunction delegates or whole classes through the [LuaObject] source generator. The API is async (LuaFunction returns ValueTask<int>, scripts can await C# tasks), so it is not an API drop-in for NLua or MoonSharp, though plain Lua 5.2 scripts mostly carry over.
how_it_is_fast: It compiles Lua to the PUC Lua 5.2 register-based instruction set (Move, LoadK, GetTabUp, Call, ForLoop...) and runs a switch-dispatch VM over a shared LuaStack of LuaValue structs (type tag, double, object reference), so numbers are not boxed. C# functions read typed arguments straight off that stack (context.GetArgument<double>) and write results back to it, avoiding the per-call object[] arrays and reflection invokes of NLua and MoonSharp's delegate binding. Execution contexts are pooled and async paths use a custom LightAsyncValueTaskMethodBuilder to keep allocations near zero (31.3 KB for 25,001 host calls in the chart).
when_to_use: .NET or Unity applications whose scripts call many small C# functions: the README chart shows a 25,001-iteration Lua loop calling a C# add() in 8.05 ms vs 36.45 ms for NLua 1.7.3 and 19.87 ms for MoonSharp 2.0.0.
Allocation-sensitive hosts (Unity frame loops, servers watching GC pauses): 31.3 KB allocated for that loop against 12,306.5 KB (NLua) and 13,887 KB (MoonSharp).
Targets where native Lua binaries or runtime IL generation are a problem: Unity IL2CPP and Mono, NativeAOT; the library is fully managed and does not emit IL.
Game scripting that wants async/await: a C# LuaFunction can await Task.Delay or other tasks and resume the Lua script afterwards; Lua coroutines can be awaited from C#.
Exposing C# types to Lua without reflection at run time, via the [LuaObject]/[LuaMember]/[LuaMetamethod] source generator.
when_not_to_use: Raw Lua compute speed: no published numbers against PUC Lua or LuaJIT (the repo's NBodyBenchmark has no results), and the only chart measures host-call overhead.

Scripts that rely on byte strings: strings are UTF-16, so string.len("あいうえお") returns 5 instead of 15 and all string functions work on UTF-16 units; not every standard library function is implemented; GC follows .NET, so collectgarbage only maps onto .NET GC calls.
Untrusted scripts that need instruction or time budgets: issue #338 (open) measured the count hook raising a 2,000,000-iteration loop from 22 ms to 72 ms (empty hook) and 127 ms (hook with checks).
Sharing one interpreter across threads: the README says LuaState is not thread-safe; #309 (open) reports a thread-safety question in [LuaObject] lazy initialization.
Hosts outside .NET: it is a managed library, not callable from C++ or Rust; Luau or PUC Lua fit native hosts.

integration.form: NuGet package (managed .NET assembly, LuaCSharp) plus a Unity package via git URL
integration.dependencies: LuaCSharp.Annotations and LuaCSharp.SourceGenerator (its own packages); Microsoft.Bcl.TimeProvider on net6.0 and netstandard2.1; System.Runtime.CompilerServices.Unsafe on netstandard2.1
integration.min_toolchain: .NET Standard 2.1 (builds for net6.0, net8.0, net10.0, netstandard2.1); Unity 2021.3+; C# 13 to build from source
integration.platforms: any .NET runtime including NativeAOT, Unity Mono and IL2CPP; single-threaded WebGL had a coroutine.yield deadlock (#327, closed); #337 (open) reports a missing System.Runtime.CompilerServices.Unsafe on Unity
integration.thread_safety: LuaState is not thread-safe (README); use one state per thread
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — Lua 5.2 scripts mostly run unchanged, but the C# API (async LuaState, LuaValue, LuaFunction delegates, [LuaObject]) differs from NLua and MoonSharp, and string semantics are UTF-16

gotchas: The README chart is stale and asymmetric: docs/Benchmark.png was last updated 2024-10-14 (v0.2-era code; add.lua went from 10,000 to 25,000 iterations that day and the C# callback API changed again in April 2025) and has not been re-run in the 13 releases since; it names no CPU, runtime or which variant (DoString or DoFile) is plotted. Lua-CSharp's add is a hand-written stack-reading callback, while NLua registers a MethodInfo (reflection invoke per call) and MoonSharp gets an auto-converted Func<double,double,double>; MoonSharp's DynValue.NewCallback and NLua's KeraLua state (lua.State) are not used. The harness uses [IterationSetup], which forces one invocation per iteration and which BenchmarkDotNet says should not be used for microbenchmarks under about 100 ms (each run here is 8-36 ms, 10 iterations, ShortRun).

Direction matters: in issue #156 (May 2025, Unity Mono on Windows, calling an empty Lua function from C# 5,000 times per frame) Lua-CSharp 0.4.2 ran at 40 fps against NLua 170 and MoonSharp 315; an unofficial 0.5 build reached 395 fps after exception-handling overhead was found in the profiler. User measurement, no hardware stated.

Open correctness bug #344 (2026-10-05): obj:Method() through a function-valued __index can receive the wrong self after a preceding metamethod call (OP_SELF register/frame reuse suspected); workaround is calling Type.Method(obj, ...) explicitly.
[LuaObject] classes reserve __index and __newindex for generated code, so those metamethods cannot be set by the user.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick Lua-CSharp when the host is .NET or Unity and you want Lua without native binaries; the catalogued Lua engines (Luau, LuaJIT Remake, Daslang) are native C/C++ VMs that a .NET host would reach only through a binding like NLua, which is exactly the interop cost this library avoids. Roto plays the same role for Rust hosts.
verified_claims_summary: First-party README chart (made 2024-10-14 with sandbox/Benchmark: BenchmarkDotNet 0.14.0 ShortRun, 10 warm-up and 10 measured single-invocation iterations, MemoryDiagnoser, net8.0, NLua 1.7.3, MoonSharp 2.0.0; CPU, runtime and plotted variant not stated): a Lua loop calling a host add(x, 1) 25,001 times took 8.05 ms in Lua-CSharp vs 36.45 ms in NLua and 19.87 ms in MoonSharp (about 4.5x and 2.5x, derived from page data), allocating 31.3 KB vs 12,306.5 KB and 13,887 KB.
status_note: Active (v0.5.7 on NuGet 2026-09-26, commits from nuskey8 and akeit0, 862 stars), MIT and fully managed, but still 0.x with C# API changes between releases and some open correctness issues.
